Attach XLA metadata to operations

Source: R/xla_metadata.R
experimental_xla_metadata_set_xla_metadata.Rd

Ports of jax.experimental.xla_metadata. XLA metadata are frontend attributes (string key value pairs) on the lowered operations, which XLA reads as hints, for example FUSE_LIMIT (a fusion boundary) or MUST_FUSE (fuse a group).

Usage

experimental_xla_metadata_set_xla_metadata(x = NULL, ..., code)

experimental_xla_metadata_fuse_limit(code)

experimental_xla_metadata_must_fuse_call(identifier)

experimental_xla_metadata_xla_metadata_call(f = NULL, ...)

experimental_xla_metadata_xla_metadata_call2(
  f = NULL,
  metadata = NULL,
  ad_metadata = "same"
)

Arguments

x

A pytree of arrays to tag, or NULL.

...

Metadata as named arguments.

code

An expression evaluated with the metadata in effect.

identifier

The fusion group.

f

A function, or NULL for a decorator.

metadata

A named list of metadata.

ad_metadata

"same" (the default), "drop", or a named list: the metadata of the computations autodiff derives from f (see Details).

Value

The tagged x, the value of code, or a function.

Details

  • experimental_xla_metadata_set_xla_metadata(x, ...) tags the operations that produce the arrays of the pytree x and returns x.

  • experimental_xla_metadata_set_xla_metadata(..., code = ) evaluates code with the metadata in effect: every operation staged meanwhile (under jit() and the other transformations that compile) is tagged. Nested uses merge, the inner value of a key winning; a value of NULL removes a key. Without x and code it returns a function that wraps a function to run with the metadata in effect (the decorator form of JAX).

  • experimental_xla_metadata_fuse_limit(code) evaluates code with FUSE_LIMIT = TRUE.

  • experimental_xla_metadata_must_fuse_call(identifier) returns a decorator that tags the operations of a function with MUST_FUSE = identifier.

  • experimental_xla_metadata_xla_metadata_call(f, ...) and experimental_xla_metadata_xla_metadata_call2(f, metadata, ad_metadata) wrap f so that its operations carry the metadata.

Values may be strings, logicals or numbers; they are attached as strings (logicals as "true" and "false", doubles as Python writes floats). Unlike JAX, which stages xla_metadata_call as a call operation tagged as a whole, jaxR tags the operations of the function directly, which XLA treats the same once it inlines the call; and the operations of the backward pass of grad() are tagged only when they are staged inside the context (ad_metadata other than "drop" is not applied).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
f <- jit(function(x) {
  y <- experimental_xla_metadata_set_xla_metadata(jnp_sin(x), my_key = "a")
  experimental_xla_metadata_fuse_limit(y * 2)
})
cat(f$lower(jnp_ones(3))$as_text())
} # }
